examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For fixed-size blocks, separate data capacity from per-block pointers. Linked allocation reserves link bytes even in the last block; indexed allocation uses a different metadata layout. Round record and index blocking factors down, then required block counts up. For free lists, account for the next-list-block pointer before counting stored block numbers.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A file has 2000 data bytes. Linked allocation uses 512-byte blocks with a 4-byte link in each. How many unused payload bytes occur in the last allocated block?

**Answer: 32.** Payload per block is 512−4=508. Three blocks hold 1524 bytes, so a fourth holds 476 remaining bytes. Unused payload=508−476=32. Pointer bytes are used metadata, not wasted payload.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Storage capacity units in these questions are usually explicitly binary. Internal fragmentation concerns allocated unused space, while external fragmentation concerns gaps between allocations.

Indirect blocks consume storage but do not themselves add file-content bytes.
